Latin word

dux

dux, ducis m.

noun, third declension

a leader, a general; a leader, a guide; in war, a commander; guide, leader

In this lexicon

  • general

    the recommended word · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. dux; Traupman 187; Traupman 320

  • leader

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 2.13.6: dux agminis virginum; Cic. de Or. 3.63: dux regendae cīvitātis (Lewis & Short)

  • tour guide

    also used · classical · Traupman 324

Examples

  • imperiī summam tenēre

    to be commander in chiefTraupman 186; cf. Cic. Rep. 2.51: cum imperiī summam rēx tenēret (Lewis & Short s.v. summa)

    In the entry for general

  • imperiī summae praeesse

    to be commander in chiefTraupman 186

    In the entry for general

  • Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus … frūstrāta custōdēs, dux agminis virginum inter tēla hostium Tiberim trānāvit

    Cloelia, a girl who was one of the hostages, slipped past her guards and, at the head of a band of girls, swam the Tiber under the enemy’s spearsLiv. 2.13.6

    In the entry for leader

  • dux itinerārius

    a tour guideTraupman 396

    In the entry for tour guide
